entities.name: Amenhotep, son of Hapu
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Amenhotep son of Hapu was a high official of Egypt’s Eighteenth Dynasty under Amenhotep III, serving as scribe, architect, and overseer on major Theban building projects. Later deified like Imhotep, he became a healing and wisdom saint of the New Kingdom and after, with statues and cult spaces soliciting his intercession.

His career shows how non-royal experts could achieve extraordinary honour through literacy and royal favour in the glittering court of Amenhotep III. Colossal statues inscribed with his name and appeals survive as evidence of personal piety directed to a deified official.

He is one of ancient Egypt’s rare commoners elevated to lasting divine cult—an emblem of scribal prestige in the New Kingdom.
